# Project Overview

## What this is

> status: ratified (D-0001, D-0043, D-0082)

A narrative fiction series built audio-first — a high-production, audiobook-like
podcast, fully voiced with foley, with visuals and other media possible later. It is a
nearly free art project made to create, not to fund: format and cadence answer to
listeners and the production process, nothing else. The register is adult — dark enough
for grown-ups, never trauma-exploitation, never stagey writing aimed at teens.

## The story in one breath

> status: ratified (D-0003, D-0007, D-0008, D-0011, D-0013, D-0014, D-0021, D-0022, D-0040, D-0053)

In a pre-modern world rooted in pre-Christian Northern European animism, the land
itself is sick — a sickness that surfaces as many small, local spirit-troubles, and
whose cause is the extraction of a ruling class that has poisoned the world. Magic is
spoken, rigorous logical proof; speaking truth precisely is the "battle." A woman who
was taken young and raised inside the empire walks back out of it, gathers a small
pseudo-family — an orphaned youth, a broken laborer, a hound — and does the long,
unglamorous, radically humanist work: sabotaging the engine of extraction, breaching
the hoards, teaching the young, and beginning the endless rebuilding of new ways to
live in a permanently changed world. History has turned this wheel before. Human
agency is what turns it back.

## The allegory and its discipline

> status: ratified (D-0011, D-0013, D-0019, D-0025, D-0030)

The structural allegory: class war in the age of global warming, plus the
post-American-empire, corporatist-AI wasteland — proprietary enclosure versus open,
shared knowledge. The discipline: the allegory is a tool, never foregrounded. Every
scene must be fully readable/hearable as pure hard-magic fantasy — genuine and
authentic, never arch or ironic (the Sanderson framing, [[influences]]). No modern
vocabulary surfaces in-world (see `data/banned-vocabulary.yaml`).

## The four axes at a glance

> status: ratified (D-0032, D-0219)

The working review framework is Sanderson's: plot, setting, character, glued by
conflict.

- **Plot** — fractal Kishōtenketsu; hub-and-spoke migration; three macro acts
  (sabotage → breach → the world after). See [[structure]].
- **Setting** — time-blurred pre-modern British Isles / Northern European animist
  world under an extractive imperial monopoly. See [[wyrd-and-frith]], [[the-empire]],
  [[regions]], [[economy]].
- **Character** — the trio + hound pseudo-family; the Archive-bearing protagonist; the
  female viewpoint apprentice; the broken veteran anchor; a centuries-removed
  scholar narrator. See [[protagonist]], [[apprentice]], [[anchor]], [[hound]],
  [[narrator]].
- **Conflict** — radical humanism (growing people and communities) versus systemic,
  incentive-driven greed; no demon king. See [[the-empire]], [[secondary-archetypes]].

## Status of this corpus

> status: ratified (D-0032)

Every claim in this canon carries a ratification status per `SCHEMA.md`. The decision
ledger (`decisions.md`) quotes the author; `open-questions.md` is the agenda of
unresolved forks. Raw sources are preserved verbatim under `sources/`.
